title: Glob and Grep are unusable — ripgrep binary missing from the worker environment
body:
Every Glob call in this session failed immediately with `ENOENT: no such file or directory, uv_spawn 'rg'` (one variant came back as `EUNKNOWN: unknown error, uv_spawn`). Grep is built on the same binary and would fail identically. Read works fine, so reading a file whose path you already know is unaffected.

This cost me nothing because the brief named `explorer/scratch_rightunbounded_proof.lean` exactly. It would cost a lot on a node where prior work has to be *located* rather than opened: my own notebook records the established P1 habit of globbing `runs/**/<Pascal>.lean` and `explorer/scratch_*.lean` before writing anything, because at least five nodes in this region have closed by retrieval rather than fresh proof. With ripgrep absent that habit is impossible to follow, and the guard correctly denies the Bash fallbacks (`find`, `ls`, `grep`), so there is no way at all to discover a parked file. A worker in that position would re-derive a proof that already exists on disk, or abandon a node that was already closed.

Worth checking whether this is specific to this machine's Claude Code install or something the harness could ship/point at, since the brief-writing side already assumes workers can find parked attempts.
